records.name: Central Orchestrator Bottleneck
records.definition: Routing every interaction through one central orchestrator that becomes a bottleneck and single point of failure.

records.name: Centralized Control
records.definition: Concentrating decision-making authority in one place so nodes cannot act independently.

records.name: Fully Decentralized Control
records.definition: Leaving control fully decentralized with no central plane, so global runtime policy cannot be coordinated.

records.name: Independent Node Decisions
records.definition: Letting each node decide independently with no agreement, so they diverge on shared state.

records.name: Local-Only Logs
records.definition: Leaving logs scattered on each host with no aggregation, so cross-service analysis is impossible.

records.name: Pure Choreography
records.definition: Coordinating a multi-step workflow purely through choreography when central orchestration is needed, scattering its logic.

records.name: Scattered Auth Implementations
records.definition: Reimplementing authentication separately in each service instead of centralizing it.

records.name: Scattered Configuration
records.definition: Spreading configuration across many services with no single source, so values drift out of sync.

records.name: Split-Brain Coordination
records.definition: Two nodes both believing they are leader and acting independently, corrupting shared state.

records.name: Agreed Single Value Across Nodes
records.definition: The ability for distributed nodes to agree on a single value despite failures.

records.name: Automatic Failover of Leadership
records.definition: The ability to automatically elect a new leader when the current one fails.

records.name: Central-Orchestrator-Free Coordination
records.definition: The ability for services to coordinate through events without a central orchestrator.

records.name: Centralized Control of Distributed Runtime
records.definition: The ability to manage a distributed runtime's behavior from one central control point.

records.name: Cross-Service Analysis
records.definition: The ability to analyze behavior across services by querying their aggregated logs.

records.name: Independent Ownership
records.definition: The ability for each node or team to own and control its part without central approval.

records.name: Ordered Multi-Step Execution
records.definition: The ability to execute the steps of a workflow in a defined order.

records.name: Single-Writer Coordination

distinctFrom.reason: Single-writer coordination makes one elected node the only writer, while leadership failover elects a new one when it fails.

records.definition: The ability to designate one writer for each unit of shared state, whether an elected node or the party a record names, so updates to it need no further coordination.

records.name: Unified Config Management
records.definition: The ability to manage all services' configuration from one place.

records.name: Unified Identity
records.definition: The ability to give users one identity recognized across all services.

records.name: Config Store
records.definition: A central store that holds configuration values for many services to read.

records.name: Coordinator
records.definition: A component that directs the steps of a multi-service workflow in order.

records.name: Identity Provider
records.definition: A central service that authenticates identities and issues credentials for others to trust.

records.name: Log Aggregation
records.definition: A facility that collects logs from many sources into one central store.

records.name: Management API
records.definition: A programmatic interface through which operators manage a distributed runtime's state.

records.name: Quorum
records.definition: The requirement that a majority of nodes agree before a decision commits.

records.name: Central Dependency Risk
records.definition: The degree to which centralizing configuration makes the whole system depend on one config source.

records.name: Centralized Coordinator Coupling
records.definition: The degree to which routing a workflow through a central coordinator couples participants to it.

records.name: Cost/Personal Data Exposure
records.definition: The degree to which aggregating all logs centrally raises storage cost and personal-data exposure.

records.name: Identity Provider Availability
records.definition: The degree to which every login depends on the central identity provider staying available.

records.name: Externalize Configuration
records.definition: A technique for moving values that vary by environment out of code into configuration read at startup.

records.name: Configuration Schema
records.definition: A technique for validating configuration against a declared schema before the system starts.
